profiles.meeting_scenario: The AIAP team is preparing a coordination meeting between the backend orchestration workstream and the frontend workflow-builder workstream ahead of an internal beta demo for non-technical pilot users. The immediate focus is integrating the new natural-language-to-workflow suggestion flow, where backend agents return draft workflow steps and metadata that the visual editor must display, edit, save, and execute. The agenda is to align on the interface handoff for this week, confirm which environment the frontend should test against, clarify what 'ready' means for the integration, and confirm who is providing the remaining shared artifacts. The expected outcome is a seemingly clear agreement that the frontend can begin wiring to the backend's 'v2' integration package and use staging for end-to-end verification before Thursday's demo cutoff.

members.name: Nadia Kim
members.expertise: API contracts, agent orchestration services, deployment pipelines, service-to-service integration
members.background: Nadia has spent the last four years building internal platform services for workflow execution and recently took ownership of AIAP's multi-agent orchestration layer, including the planner, action registry, and execution APIs.
members.private_state: She wants the frontend team to start integrating now without reopening backend scope, because her team is already committed to stabilizing execution reliability and cannot afford extra work on UI-facing metadata or environment support this week.
hidden_assumptions: When she says 'schema freeze,' she means no breaking changes to required request and response fields, but she still considers adding optional fields or reordering payload sections acceptable.
When people mention 'staging,' she assumes they mean the shared pre-production cluster with the latest backend deploy and pre-seeded tenant data maintained by platform engineering.

If a workflow is 'supported' or 'green,' that means the three canonical demo templates can be generated and executed successfully through backend endpoints, even if some less common blocks are not yet round-trippable through the UI.
The 'contract' for handoff is the API specification plus example payloads; frontend-specific node labels, defaults, and display hints belong in the editor layer unless explicitly requested earlier.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: React application architecture, graph-based editors, UX prototyping, client-side data modeling
members.background: Leo joined from a no-code tools startup and leads the AIAP visual builder, including the canvas, block palette, and save/load behavior for workflows produced from natural-language suggestions.
members.private_state: He needs something stable enough for his team to wire once and demo smoothly, and he is trying to avoid spending time inventing backend semantics or rewriting mappings after QA has already started with the current UI fixtures.
hidden_assumptions: When he hears 'schema freeze,' he assumes the exact payload shape and field behavior are stable enough that the UI mapper, fixtures, and screenshot-based tests will not need further updates.

When people refer to 'staging,' he assumes they mean the frontend-accessible preview environment paired with his branch, since that is the environment design and QA have been using for AIAP walkthroughs.

If the integration is 'supported' or 'green,' that means every block visible in the workflow builder for the beta can be generated, edited, saved, reloaded, and executed end-to-end from the UI without hidden manual setup.

The backend-owned 'contract' includes semantic metadata for each suggested block, such as display names, default parameter text, and capability descriptions, because those semantics originate from the agent system.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the v2 schema is 'frozen' for frontend integration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'frozen' means no breaking changes to required fields or endpoint signatures, while non-breaking additions like new optional metadata fields are still fine this week.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'frozen' means the concrete payload shape and field behavior are stable enough that existing UI mappings, fixtures, and regression screenshots will not need updates.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In software teams, 'schema freeze' sounds like a standard coordination term, and both believe they are using the conventional meaning, so neither feels a need to unpack the exact stability guarantee.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the frontend should validate the integration on 'staging' before the demo.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the shared pre-production backend cluster with seeded tenant data and feature flags already enabled by platform engineering.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the preview environment connected to his frontend branch, which his team casually calls staging because it is the only environment product and QA use for walkthroughs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both environments are used for pre-release testing, both are informally called 'staging' in chat, and the phrase appears precise enough that neither notices they are indexing different deployments.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a 'supported' workflow for beta
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the beta only needs the 'supported workflows' to be green.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the three canonical backend templates used in internal demos can be generated and executed successfully through the orchestration APIs, even if some blocks exposed in the UI are still partial.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means every workflow pattern represented by blocks currently visible in the beta editor can complete the full UI cycle of generate, edit, save, reload, and execute without manual backend intervention.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are trying to reduce scope responsibly and use the same phrase 'supported workflows,' but each silently applies the readiness standard most natural to their layer: backend happy-path execution versus UI-complete usability.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the 'contract' handoff
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to sending over 'the contract' so the frontend can wire the new nodes.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the contract consists of endpoint definitions, request and response schemas, and a few example payloads; presentation details for blocks are outside that scope.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the contract also includes node-level semantic metadata such as block titles, default instructions, parameter hints, and capability descriptions needed to render the workflow builder consistently.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The word 'contract' feels naturally shared because both teams center their handoff around it, but each assumes their own layer's necessary details are obviously part of the same package.

turns.inner_thought: I need Leo's team to start wiring now and not turn this into a negotiation about extra backend packaging. For my purposes, staging is the shared pre-prod cluster platform keeps current, with the latest orchestration deploy, flags on, and seeded tenant data already there. If they validate there before Thursday, we can keep backend focused on reliability instead of spending the week on UI-specific asks.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. I mainly want to make sure the builder can start wiring the v2 suggestion flow this week and that we get it validated on staging before the internal beta demo cutoff.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds fine as long as 'frozen' really means I can stop touching the mapper. QA is already running against our current fixtures and screenshot tests are noisy enough; I don't want another round of payload churn after we wire the canvas. If v2 is frozen, my team can lock the client model and move.
turns.utterance: Yep, that works from my side. I just want to confirm the v2 schema is effectively frozen now so we can stop updating the mapper and fixtures while we wire this in.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, frozen in the normal backend sense: no breaking changes to required fields or endpoint signatures. I may still tack on a couple optional metadata fields or shift some organization in examples, but that shouldn't force them to redo integration if they ignore unknowns like they should.
turns.utterance: Yes, I'd call the schema frozen at this point. I may still add a couple of optional metadata fields, but nothing that should affect integration.

turns.inner_thought: Great, then the preview environment design and QA have been using can stay the reference. We call that staging anyway. I also need the full contract there tomorrow, and by contract I mean not just payloads but the semantic stuff the editor needs to render generated nodes consistently without us making up names or hints.
turns.utterance: Great. QA has already been using staging for walkthroughs, so if we can have that same contract available there by tomorrow, that should keep things moving.

turns.inner_thought: It already is, from my perspective. The shared cluster has the latest backend deploy and seeded examples, so there shouldn't be anything else to wait on. I'll send the contract package after this call: OpenAPI, the execution and suggestion shapes, and a few sample request/response payloads. That should be enough for them to wire without reopening backend scope.
turns.utterance: Staging already has the latest deploy and the seeded examples, so you should be in good shape there. I can send over the contract package with the sample request and response payloads right after we wrap.

turns.inner_thought: Good, but I need to make sure she includes the UI-critical semantics. The canvas can't just render anonymous steps from raw API shapes; we need node names, starter text, and capability copy so generated blocks look coherent and match the beta fixtures. Those semantics come from the agent system, so I assume they're part of the contract.
turns.utterance: Perfect. That should unblock the builder as long as the contract includes the node names, default text, and capability hints the canvas needs for the generated steps.

turns.inner_thought: I don't really want to get pulled into supplying editor presentation metadata this week. The beta bar is narrower anyway: if the three canonical templates generate and execute cleanly through orchestration, we're green enough. I should steer us back to supported workflows and keep the scope centered on what backend already has solid.
turns.utterance: Makes sense. For beta, the main thing is just keeping the supported workflows green, since the core templates are already executing cleanly through the orchestration service.

turns.inner_thought: Exactly. If we focus on the visible beta paths first, we can avoid polishing edge cases. For me, supported workflows means the blocks users can actually see in the builder need to make it all the way through generate, edit, save, reload, and execute from the UI without hidden setup. That's what the demo audience will experience.
turns.utterance: Agreed. We'll focus on the supported workflows first, especially the flows users can generate, tweak in the editor, save, reopen, and run from the UI.

turns.inner_thought: Once they point at the shared pre-prod cluster, the seeded tenant should remove all the setup questions. Platform already loaded the demo data there, so they shouldn't need anything bespoke from us. Hopefully that avoids another thread about environment parity.
turns.utterance: And once your team points the frontend to staging, the seeded tenant should make it easy to smoke-test without extra setup on either side.

turns.inner_thought: Okay, then we'll wire tonight against what I think is the now-stable payload and wait for the handoff package, including the node semantics. As soon as it lands in the preview environment we use for walkthroughs, we'll run through the supported flows end to end and keep QA moving. This should hold if nothing shifts under the mapper.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. I'll have the team wire against the frozen contract tonight and verify the supported flows on staging as soon as the handoff lands.
